full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim Jr: This is an application filed by the decree holder-opposite party Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation for discharging the rule. 

 3. Short fact, for disposal of this application is that the judgment-debtor herein look loan of Taka 5,78,000 from House Building Finance Corporation (HBFC). The loan was payable within 30 years but due to non-payment of the loan amount it stands upto Taka 13,12,386.43 principal with interest. Subsequently, the decree holder-HBFC served a legal notice on 12-6-1997 and asked the judgment-debtor to take the advantage of 15% incentive on payment of the outstanding loan amount, but the judgment-debtor did not response to the offer. Thereafter, the House Building Finance Corporation filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1998 under Article 27(1) of the President Order No. 7 of 1973 for realization of outstanding amount of Taka 13,12,386.43. After service of notice upon the loanee-judgment-debtor, he filed an application for re-scheduling of his loan amount. Bangladesh House Building Finance Corporation asked the judgment-debtor to make payment Taka 1,35,000 and accordingly he paid the said amount against the loan case on 26-6-2001. On receiving of the said amount the House Building Finance Corporation filed a compromise petition for payment of the loan stating that the judgment-debtor shall re-pay the loan amount in 258 installments, each installment is of Taka 7,790.90. The payment of the installments were scheduled to be start from 1-7-2001. Accordingly, said miscellaneous case was compromised between the parties and same was disposed on compromise by the judgment dated 7-8-2001. Subsequently, the decree-holder, House Building Finance Corporation filed Execution Case No. 1 of 2004 to realize the decreetal amount of Taka 15,45,042.13 by selling mortgaged property and to execute the decree dated 14-8-2001 passed on the basis on compromise petition. 

 4. During pendency of the execution case the judgment-debtor filed an application under Order XXXIV, rule 14 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the execution case because the decree-holder obtain money decree and there is no provision for realizing the decreetal amount by selling the mortgaged property. House Building Finance Corporation deemed to be the decree-holder under Article 27(7)(b) or under Article 9 of the President Order No.7 of 1973 filed the present execution case without instituting a suit for selling the mortgage property. In the execution case, judgment-debtor filed an application under Order XXXIV, rule 14 of the Code of Civil Procedure and same was rejected by order dated 10-6-2004 passed by the learned District Judge, Kishoreganj. 

 Pending hearing of the Rule, let all further proceedings of the Decree Execution (House building loan) Case No. 1 of 2004, of the Court of District Judge, Kishoreganj be stayed for a period of 4(four) months."
